title: PERBANDINGAN EFEK ANTARA CAIRAN RINGER LAKTAT, KOMBINASI RINGER LAKTAT DAN HES 6%, SERTA RINGER LAKTAT DAN GELOFUSINE PADA RESUSITASI LANJUT PASIEN SYOK HEMORAGIK=COMPARISON OF EFFECTS BETWEEN RINGER LACTATE SOLUTION, COMBINATION OF RINGER LACTATE AND HES 6%, AND RINGER LACTATE AND GELOFUSINE IN ADVANCED RESUSCITATION OF PATIENTS WITH HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK
INCIDENCE, PREVALENCE AND KNOWLEDGE OF TYPE II DIABETES MELLITUS AMONG ADULT PATIENTS ABOVE 45 YEARS IN BOMET COUNTY.
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is an increasing health problem worldwide and in sub-Saharan Africa, where many cases remain undiagnosed until complications arise. Millions of adults are living with diabetes and many of them are unaware of their condition. Risk increases with age, which makes adults above 45 years an important group in hospital diabetes clinics such as Longisa County Referral Hospital in Bomet County.OBJECTIVE: This review used existing evidence on the incidence, prevalence and level of knowledge of type 2 diabetes mellitus among adult patients above 45 years attending specifically Longisa County Referral Hospital. METHODOLOGY: This systematic review was guided by the PRISMA 2020 framework. PubMed/PMC, Google and African Journals Online were referred for studies published between January 2010 and October 2026. The studies were checked for the eligibility criteria, data extracted with a structured form, quality appraised for cross-sectional studies, and findings synthesised. Results: Fifteen studies were able to meet the inclusion criteria. No study reported the incidence of type 2 diabetes mellitus in Kenya or at Longisa County Referral Hospital, and none reported prevalence specifically for patients above 45 years at Longisa. National data showed an age-related diabetes prevalence, with odds of diabetes higher at 60–69 years than in younger adults. Knowledge of diabetes was generally poor; few community members had good knowledge. At Longisa, access to services and equipment, cost of glucometers and the need for continuous health education were the major concerns. Conclusion: Evidence on the burden and knowledge of type 2 diabetes mellitus among adults above 45 years at Longisa County Referral Hospital is slim. Facility-based incidence and prevalence studies and knowledge assessment are needed to guide diabetes screening, patient education and care in Bomet County.

title: Multidisciplinary management of disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculous meningitis and active hepatitis B in a critically ill pregnant woman in the third trimester: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Tuberculous meningitis (TBM) in pregnancy is rare but life-threatening, with substantial maternal and fetal risks. Third-trimester disseminated tuberculosis involving the central nervous system with concurrent active hepatitis B infection has scarcely been reported, particularly among remote pastoral populations with limited healthcare access. This report highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of this triple comorbidity and underscores the value of multidisciplinary team (MDT) management in such complex scenarios. Case presentation A 24-year-old pastoralist at 30 weeks of gestation presented with headache, vomiting, fever, and nuchal rigidity. Cerebrospinal fluidanalysis confirmed TBM, and chest computed tomography revealed diffuse miliary nodules suggestive of hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis. Serology was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, e-antigen, and core antibody, indicating active viral replication. Given life-threatening intracranial hypertension [intracranial pressure (ICP) > 330 mmH 2 O] in late pregnancy, osmotic agents were withheld for fetal safety, and lumbar cisternal drainage was performed. An MDT comprising respiratory medicine, obstetrics, hepatology, pharmacy, and critical care nursing specialties was assembled. Anti-tuberculosis therapy was intensified to isoniazid, rifampicin, linezolid, and moxifloxacin; ethambutol was discontinued due to fetal optic neuritis, and tenofovir was added for hepatitis B management. Following stabilization, the patient was transferred to a higher-level facility at 35 weeks of gestation and underwent cesarean section at 36 weeks, delivering a live preterm female infant (2320 g, 1-min Apgar score of 8). Both mother and neonate were discharged without complications on December 1, 2025. Conclusions This case demonstrates that early recognition, individualized anti-tuberculosis regimens, and coordinated multidisciplinary collaboration are critical for achieving favorable outcomes in pregnant patients with disseminated tuberculosis complicated by TBM and concurrent hepatitis B infection. The successful management relied on integrated critical care and a multidisciplinary approach, which proved effective even in resource-limited pastoral settings.
